description: Car rental booking platform aggregating 600+ suppliers across 150+ countries and 30,000+ pickup locations, with 18+ years in the industry; its affiliate program pays partners a 60% revenue share of the commission EconomyBookings earns on each completed booking.

evidence.summary: EconomyBookings' own affiliate page states: '60% of every commission we earn goes straight to you. No caps, no limits.' and 'Earn 60% of every commission on every completed booking. No minimums, no caps.' — an explicit no-earnings-cap statement, so commission_cap is uncapped. The 60% is a revenue share of the platform's own commission (worked example on the page: a €350 booking at a 15% platform commission of €52.50 pays the partner €31.50, plus €9.84 on add-ons).

The page specifies a 30-day cookie, free signup in about 2 minutes, a dedicated partner manager, and explicitly courts bloggers and influencers ('Monetize your travel content on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or your blog'); it reports 600+ active partners — a partner count in the hundreds, so creator_saturation stays unknown under the absolute-terms rule.

The page lists 18+ years in the industry, 600+ suppliers, 150+ countries and 30,000+ locations, and a 'Top 500 Largest Companies in Latvia 2023–2024' award among its recognitions, supporting the Latvia base.

name: EconomyBookings

reasons.compensation: 60% revenue share of the platform's commission with an explicit 'No caps, no limits' statement on the brand's own page — the strongest verified compensation terms in this group.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate email is published; partners get a dedicated manager only after signup, so contact access is mid-range.
reasons.credibility: 18+ years operating, 600+ suppliers, 150+ countries, industry awards and a published partner-payout track record.
reasons.niche_fit: Car rentals are a core travel-creator monetisation category, and the brand's own page explicitly targets travel bloggers and social creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open self-serve signup on the brand's own page, live in about 5 minutes with no technical skills required.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The official affiliate page has a dedicated 'Bloggers & Influencers' track naming Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and blogs as monetisable channels.

description: British slow-fashion brand founded in 2016, designing vintage-inspired women's clothing in-house in the UK in an inclusive size range; a Certified B Corporation selling direct at joanieclothing.com, with affiliate programs on Awin for the US and UK.

evidence.summary: Joanie Clothing's official Awin merchant profile (US program) lists among its reasons to promote: 'A competitive commission structure with uncapped earnings' — an explicit no-cap statement on the network's own merchant page, so commission_cap is uncapped. The profile also notes a dedicated affiliate team, regular promotional offers and content to promote, and a separate dedicated UK program.
Lasso's directory lists the Joanie affiliate program at 6% per sale with a 30-day cookie.

Joanie's own About page confirms the brand opened its virtual doors in October 2016, designs everything in-house from its UK HQ, is a Certified B Corporation, and sells only direct at joanieclothing.com in an inclusive size range.

name: Joanie Clothing

reasons.compensation: A modest 6% rate, but the Awin merchant profile explicitly states uncapped earnings, lifting compensation above rate-only peers.
reasons.contact_access: Application runs through Awin with a dedicated affiliate team named on the profile; no public email is published.
reasons.credibility: Certified B Corporation, operating since 2016, designing in-house in the UK and selling direct worldwide.
reasons.niche_fit: Vintage-inspired slow fashion with an inclusive size range and a strong storytelling angle — a natural fit for fashion creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application via Awin, with both US and UK programs available.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Awin profile promises regular promotional offers and content to promote plus a dedicated affiliate team supporting publishers.

description: Free-walking-tour platform connecting travellers with local guides in 100+ countries; its open affiliate program pays 50% of GuruWalk's own commission per traveller booked through the affiliate's link, and anyone can join free with no website required.

evidence.summary: GuruWalk's own support article states the affiliate commission structure: 'High commissions: We offer one of the most profitable commission structures in the free tour sector (50% of our commission per traveller)' — a revenue share of GuruWalk's per-traveller commission, not a percentage of a booking price, since the tours are free to book and GuruWalk monetises PRO tours.

GuruWalk's own support article states: 'You don't need to have tourist accommodation, a blog or a website... Anyone can become an affiliate and achieve results by promoting tours via WhatsApp, social media or any other channel. The program is open to everyone.' Joining is completely free; signup is at guruwalk.com/afiliados.
GuruWalk's own support contact page publishes three affiliate and partnership emails: partnerships@guruwalk.com, afiliados@guruwalk.com and affiliates@guruwalk.com.

GuruWalk's affiliate terms name the operator as GuruWalk S.L., domiciled at Calle Guillem de Castro 9, 46007 Valencia, Spain, and confirm joining the affiliate programme is free of charge with no ongoing costs.

name: GuruWalk

reasons.compensation: 50% of GuruWalk's commission per traveller is a high revenue share, though the underlying per-traveller commission on free tours is small, so absolute earnings per booking are modest.
reasons.contact_access: Three published affiliate/partnership emails on the brand's own support site — top-band contact access.
reasons.credibility: Established platform (GuruWalk S.L., Valencia) operating free tours in 100+ countries with published affiliate terms.
reasons.niche_fit: Free walking tours in 100+ countries are highly promotable travel content, especially for city-guide and budget-travel creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to everyone, free to join, no website or business required, per the brand's own programme requirements article.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own support docs explicitly bless promotion via social media and WhatsApp with no website needed — direct evidence of a creator-friendly program.

description: Designer clothing rental platform offering subscriptions, one-time rentals and resale of designer apparel; its affiliate program runs on Impact and its partnerships team is reachable at a published email.

evidence.summary: Rent the Runway's own partnerships page publishes partnerships@renttherunway.com 'For partnership opportunities', and the site footer carries an 'Affiliate Program — Join Now' link pointing to app.impact.com, confirming the affiliate program runs on Impact.

Kit's affiliate-program roundup lists Rent The Runway at 7% commission (in an older ShareASale context; the brand's own site now routes affiliate signup through Impact). Lasso's affiliate directory independently lists Rent the Runway at 7% per sale with a 30-day cookie.

name: Rent the Runway

reasons.compensation: 7% per sale per two independent directories — a mid-range fashion rate; no cap statement found, so the cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: A dedicated partnerships email is published on the brand's own partnerships page, alongside the Impact application route.
reasons.credibility: A large, long-established US consumer platform with subscriptions, rentals, resale and investor-relations presence.
reasons.niche_fit: Designer fashion rental is a staple of fashion-creator content (hauls, occasion dressing, subscription reviews).
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications run through Impact; approval is at the brand's discretion, so availability is good but not instant.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A public affiliate program on Impact plus a partnerships page courting collaborators shows an active creator channel.

description: Digital-first size-inclusive fashion brand founded in 2021 in Los Angeles, selling women's clothing in sizes 10–30 through its own site; its affiliate program on Awin pays 6%–15% on every confirmed sale with a 30-day cookie.

evidence.summary: BloomChic's Awin merchant profile states: 'Commission: Earn 6%-15% on every confirmed sale', average earnings of approximately $8 per sale, a 30-day cookie, and publishes the contact affiliate@bloomchic.com; approved promotion channels are organic only, including blogs, content websites and social media platforms. The top of the brand's own published range (15%) is recorded as the rate, with the full range documented here.
CB Insights lists BloomChic as founded in 2021 and headquartered in Los Angeles, California, specialising in plus-size women's clothing in sizes 10–30.

name: BloomChic

reasons.compensation: 6%–15% per confirmed sale on the brand's own Awin profile — the top of the range is solid for fashion; no cap statement found.
reasons.contact_access: A dedicated affiliate email (affiliate@bloomchic.com) is published on the program profile.
reasons.credibility: Founded 2021 in Los Angeles with institutional backing (L Catterton investment reported) and a large social following.
reasons.niche_fit: Size-inclusive fashion for sizes 10–30 is an underserved, high-engagement creator niche, especially on TikTok.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through Awin with marketing tools, coupons and data feeds provided.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The Awin profile encourages creative freedom (photos, collages, reviews) and names social media as an approved channel.

description: UK adaptive-clothing brand (The Able Label Ltd) selling easy-dress clothing designed for people with limited mobility and dressing difficulties; its affiliate program pays 10% of sales value and is tracked through Affiliatly.

evidence.summary: The Able Label's own affiliate terms state affiliates are 'entitled to receive 10% of the sales value of purchase/order placed on the website (excluding tax and shipping)' via their unique URL, with commission tracking through Affiliatly and payment into the affiliate's chosen account on the last Friday of every month; the agreement is with The Able Label Ltd and governed by the laws of England.

name: The Able Label

reasons.compensation: 10% of sales value (excluding tax and shipping) stated in the brand's own affiliate terms — a fair mid-range fashion rate.
reasons.contact_access: No affiliate email is published in the terms; joining runs through the Affiliatly registration route only.
reasons.credibility: An established UK limited company with a defined product niche and full published affiliate terms and conditions.
reasons.niche_fit: Adaptive clothing is a small but genuinely underserved fashion niche with loyal audiences (disability, ageing, post-surgery dressing).
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open registration under published terms, with monthly payouts once the minimum is reached.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A formal affiliate program with published terms exists, but there is no visible creator community or ambassador layer on the brand's pages.

description: Vintage-inspired women's clothing and accessories retailer known for indie designs and size-inclusive ranges; its long-running affiliate program is hosted on ShareASale, with older listings also placing it on CJ and Rakuten.

evidence.summary: Kit's affiliate roundup lists ModCloth at 7% on ShareASale, while other directories list 5% (Empire Flippers' fashion affiliate guide; bloggerteck's clothing program list) and one lists a 5%–20% range (tasklanding). Because published sources conflict on the current rate, commission_rate is null and the conflict is documented here.

AffiliateTips' ShareASale fashion list gives ModCloth's ShareASale signup (merchantID 45519) plus a LinkShare/Rakuten signup link and quotes 5% commission (2% on deals and discounts) with a 30-day cookie — confirming the program's network presence and adding to the rate conflict.

name: ModCloth

reasons.compensation: Published rates conflict (5% vs 7% vs a 5%–20% range), so no rate is recorded and compensation scores low until the brand confirms current terms.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate contact found; access is through the ShareASale merchant page only.
reasons.credibility: A well-known US online fashion retailer operating for many years with a large catalogue.
reasons.niche_fit: Vintage-inspired, size-inclusive women's fashion with a distinctive aesthetic that suits style creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application via ShareASale with reported fast approval.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A long-running network affiliate program with banners, links and a product datafeed reported by directories, but no public creator program page of its own.

description: Amsterdam-based travel eSIM provider founded in 2023 offering free and paid global mobile data in 170+ countries through one app; its own affiliate program gives bloggers, influencers and travel creators a personal link and discount code.

evidence.summary: Firsty's own affiliate page invites bloggers, influencers and creators, and travel/lifestyle creators specifically: affiliates get a personal link and exclusive discount code, 'promote with full creative freedom', and track signups and commissions; applications are reviewed by the Firsty team. The page publishes no commission percentage.

OffersPilot's eSIM affiliate roundup lists the Firsty Affiliate Program at 15% commission with a 30-day cookie and coverage in 170+ countries; as the single directory source for the rate, it is recorded as publicly reported.
Firsty's own press release states the company was founded in 2023 by ex-Adyen technical product managers and is headquartered in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

name: Firsty

reasons.compensation: 15% commission per OffersPilot's directory (30-day cookie) — a competitive eSIM rate, though Firsty's own page does not publish the figure.
reasons.contact_access: A general support email appears on the partner pages; there is no dedicated affiliate inbox published.
reasons.credibility: Amsterdam startup founded 2023 with institutional seed funding and award recognition in the MVNO/eSIM space.
reasons.niche_fit: Travel eSIM is a natural, repeatable recommendation for travel creators, and Firsty's free tier lowers the barrier for audiences.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Public application on the brand's own page, subject to team approval.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own affiliate page is written directly for influencers and travel/lifestyle creators, with creative freedom promised.

description: Car rental broker founded in 1954, comparing rental prices across 180+ countries and 24,000+ locations; its affiliate offer runs through Travelpayouts, with rates that vary by the Auto Europe domain used and the affiliate's audience region.

evidence.summary: Travelpayouts' own brands directory lists AutoEurope (EU, UK) at 4.4%–8% — 'The partner commission depends on the domain where the booking is made: 4.4% for autoeurope.co.uk, 8% for all other domains' — with a 30-day cookie lifetime.

Lasso lists the Auto Europe affiliate offer at 2.4%–5.6% per sale with a 7-day cookie (the US/Canada-audience variant described in Travelpayouts materials), while Auto Europe's own UK affiliate page says commissions 'normally start at 5%'. Because the applicable rate depends on domain and audience and the sources describe different schedules, commission_rate is null and the schedules are documented here.
Travelpayouts' AutoEurope posts describe joining the program to 'earn up to 8% commission on car rentals in over 24,000 locations across 180 countries'.

name: Auto Europe

reasons.compensation: Documented schedules run 4.4%–8% (EU/UK offer) and 2.4%–5.6% (US/CA offer) of the booking amount — usable, but no single rate applies, so none is recorded.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate email found; contact runs through the Travelpayouts network dashboard.
reasons.credibility: Operating since 1954 with inventory in 180+ countries and 24,000+ locations — one of the longest-established car rental brokers.
reasons.niche_fit: Car rental is a standard travel-content monetisation category, though the program is pitched mainly at website owners rather than social creators.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to join through Travelpayouts with easy approval reported by directories.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Program materials target content-led travel affiliates and bloggers; there is no dedicated creator or ambassador layer.

description: The world's largest operator of open-top hop-on hop-off sightseeing bus tours, founded in 1991 in London and operating in more than 20 cities worldwide; its affiliate program on Travelpayouts pays 9% of the completed booking price with a 28-day cookie.

evidence.summary: Travelpayouts' own Big Bus Tours program page states: 'The partner reward is 9% of the experience cost', a 28-day cookie lifetime, an average order price of $137, worldwide geotargeting and a dedicated support team; it notes only website owners can earn with this tours and activities program.
Niche Site Project's travel affiliate roundup lists Big Bus Tours as founded in 1991 and based in London, UK, operating hop-on hop-off sightseeing tours in major cities across four continents.

name: Big Bus Tours

reasons.compensation: 9% of the completed booking price on an average order of $137 per Travelpayouts' own program page — a solid tours rate.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate email found; support runs through Travelpayouts.
reasons.credibility: Founded 1991 in London and described by Travelpayouts as arguably the world's largest open-top sightseeing tour operator.
reasons.niche_fit: City sightseeing tours are easy, visual travel content for destination creators, though the program is aimed at website owners.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to Travelpayouts publishers with ready-to-use links and a link generator.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The network program page describes link tools for website owners; no creator-specific program or ambassador evidence found.
